attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing analytic input is a richness or separation theorem for the locked Wilson core: can reflected Wilson hairpin observables realize collar OS correlations above a prescribed nonrank-one boundary damping level |B_{12}|, or are all realized correlations automatically bounded by the boundary Gram factor?
steps: Start with fixed-collar reflection positivity: for any coefficients c, c^*N^{\delta}c\ge0. Entrywise cutoff removal at fixed \delta preserves this by the closed cone argument, so N^{\delta}->N with N\ge0.
Assume the collar trace does not alter the algebra except through a boundary Gram factor B, so N=B\circ M. This is the precise place where the same-theory condition is tested rather than assumed.
Normalize a two-observable realized block by positive diagonal congruence, giving B_{11}=B_{22}=M_{11}=M_{22}=1. Positivity of B gives |B_{12}|\le1 and positivity of N gives |N_{12}|\le1.

The intended target block is M_{12}=N_{12}/B_{12}. Its determinant is 1-|N_{12}/B_{12}|^2. Therefore the target OS block is positive exactly when the realized collar correlation is no larger than the boundary Gram correlation: |N_{12}|\le|B_{12}|.

If |B_{12}|<1 but the Wilson core cannot realize |N_{12}|>|B_{12}|, then the nonrank-one boundary sector is not yet a falsifier. If such a pair is realized, the determinant is negative and the same-theory OS bridge fails.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-dimensional determinant calculation is valid, but it proves only a conditional detector. It does not prove that Yang-Mills Wilson observables realize the needed two-by-two block, nor does it prove that the multiplicative B-factor model exhausts all collar-collapse defects.

assumptions: For every finite collar family F_i^{\delta}, cutoff removal gives an OS-positive matrix N^{\delta}_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i^{\delta},F_j^{\delta}) and N^{\delta}->N entrywise.
The intended boundary matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) exists as a distributional trace of the same Wilson observables.
The only remaining collar-collapse defect in the Wilson sector is multiplicative on each finite block: N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}, with B_{ii}>0 and B positive semidefinite as a boundary Gram matrix.
The two-observable block is normalized so M_{11}=M_{22}=1 and B_{11}=B_{22}=1; the same argument applies after diagonal rescaling when diagonals are positive.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive gauge-invariant Wilson collar Schwinger forms S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i^{\delta},F_j^{\delta}) with a,L removed first at fixed collar distance \delta>0

target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions on the locked gauge-invariant Wilson algebra after the collar observables are traced to the reflection plane without adding boundary counterterms
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, mediated by finite reflected quadratic forms and a boundary trace map T_\delta F -> F

same-theory condition: the boundary trace map identifies the same Wilson observable before and after collar collapse; any multiplicative anomaly must be an already-locked diagonal congruence or must pass every realized determinant test in the target algebra

equations.label: multiplicative boundary factorization
equations.valid_when: The collar limit has no additive boundary contact term and all residual reflected Wilson hairpin effects enter as a finite-block multiplicative boundary Gram factor.

equations.label: two-by-two target determinant
equations.valid_when: The two-observable target OS block is Hermitian and normalized by positive diagonal entries.

equations.label: realized damping detector
equations.valid_when: B_{12}\ne0 and the multiplicative factorization holds for the realized two-observable block.

equations.label: cross-ratio obstruction
equations.valid_when: The normalized boundary Gram entries are nonzero and phases have been removed by diagonal unitary rescaling.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find locked Wilson collar observables with normalized fixed-collar limit |N_{12}|>|B_{12}|. Then the collar matrices are positive, but the intended same-theory boundary matrix has negative determinant.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma replaces the overstrong universal Schur-multiplier demand with a realized finite-block detector: it tells exactly when a nontrivial boundary Gram factor actually breaks OS positivity for the locked Yang-Mills Wilson algebra.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let a locked Wilson collar core have fixed-collar OS limits N^{\delta}\ge 0 and suppose collar collapse produces a positive normalized boundary Gram factor B with N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij} for the intended same-theory boundary OS matrix M. For any realized two-observable block with unit diagonal normalization, the same-theory passage is valid exactly when |M_{12}|\le 1, equivalently |N_{12}|\le |B_{12}|. Thus a nonrank-one boundary Gram factor is a falsifier only if the locked Wilson core realizes an OS correlation exceeding the boundary Gram damping threshold.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from the closed-cone topology route if a realized Wilson two-block with |N_{12}|>|B_{12}| is found, or if mixed Wilson traces require boundary counterterms not present in the locked target algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge lemma if one proves boundary factorization plus the realized correlation bound |N_{12}|\le|B_{12}| for a dense Wilson core, or alternatively proves B has only diagonal-congruence rank-one form.
control_decision.reason: The branch made new progress by replacing an abstract rich-cone hypothesis with an explicit determinant threshold that can be attacked analytically or by constructing a Wilson hairpin falsifier.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge now has a finite realized determinant sublemma: after fixed-collar closed-cone passage, same-theory trace positivity reduces on two-observable Wilson blocks to |N_{12}|\le|B_{12}| when a multiplicative boundary Gram factor is present.
The locked Wilson algebra must be rich enough either to detect nonrank-one boundary Gram damping by an actual determinant test or to prove a structural bound preventing such detection.
The topology must control fixed-collar reflected forms plus the mixed Wilson trace map; abstract OS-cone closure alone is no longer the bottleneck.

falsifiers: A concrete two-loop hairpin family with normalized |B_{12}|<1 and realized fixed-collar |N_{12}|>|B_{12}| is a determinant falsifier of the same-theory OS passage.
An additive boundary contact term with zero diagonal but nonzero off-diagonal would falsify the positive-contact reduction used before the multiplicative detector.

If the cutoff-removal topology controls fixed-collar probes but not the \delta->0 trace of mixed reflected Wilson products, then the closed-cone argument is valid only on the collar algebra and not on the intended continuum algebra.

If quotienting or renormalizing Wilson loops at the reflection plane changes B by an unrecorded boundary counterterm, the positivity proof may describe a modified theory rather than the same Yang-Mills target.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 195 turns the previous richness caveat into a precise two-by-two inequality. A nonrank-one boundary Gram factor is not automatically a same-theory falsifier; it becomes one exactly when the realized collar OS correlation exceeds the damping supplied by the boundary Gram entry. This is useful because it gives a valid finite determinant experiment: compute or bound |B_{12}| from the boundary hairpin OPE and compare it with an actually realized |N_{12}| from locked Wilson collar observables. The bridge has moved from universal Schur-multiplier overclaiming to a concrete realized-correlation threshold.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Model two reflected Wilson hairpins sharing one reflection-plane footprint. Derive the leading boundary OPE contribution to B_{12}, then test whether a locked pair of collar loop observables can realize |N_{12}| above that value after diagonal normalization.
